**1. TL;DR — six themes, clustered**

- **Election day, and the tape is pricing it before the voters do.** Nov 3 is the US midterms — all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats.
- Polls close from ~18:00 ET, so **no result lands before the cash close**.
- Options price ~0.86% for the session and 1.85% into Nov 6; a Democratic House is priced at 91-93%. The bigger risk today is the **AI trade repricing**, not the count:
- the Nasdaq-100 fell 1.36% Monday into correction territory while the Dow rose 0.43%, and a Democratic Congress would put the data-centre buildout under more scrutiny.
- **Software and consumer-tech earnings are the day's dominant mover — and the market is paying for revenue quality, not for beats.** Down:
- **ADEA -20.2%**, **ZBRA -16.4%**, **SHOP -15.4%**, **DT -13.8%**, **DOCN -3.1%**, **PLTR -6.3%**, **AAPL -3.9%**. Up: **BLZE +34.4%**, **AEHR +18.5%**, **RVTY +10.2%**, **GRAB +10.5%**, **FISV +10.0%**.
- Nearly every decliner *beat or raised*:
- Adeia reiterated its $600M long-term target while cutting FY26 revenue, Zebra beat and raised and still fell, Dynatrace beat on EPS and revenue but trimmed FY guidance.
- The tape is trading **guidance credibility, not headlines**.
- **Chips are bouncing, and AMD is the referee tonight.** **INTC +3.7%** pre-market after -8.8% Monday, **NVDA +2.1%**, **LSCC +10.6%**, **AEHR +18.5%**, **HLIT +17.6%**.
- **AMD reports after the close** on consensus **$13.08-13.09B revenue (+42% y/y)** and **$1.95 adjusted EPS**, with the ~56% gross-margin guide and Client revenue the lines to watch.
- **Oracle's $20B raise has stopped hurting —
- but the stock sits only +3.4% above the offering price.** ORCL priced **86,206,897 shares at $116** (11.2% below the Oct 30 close) plus **$10B of senior notes at 7.00-8.65%**, closing Nov 4.
- ORCL fell **8.8%** Monday and is now **+0.6% at $119.95** pre-market. The dilution is priced; the margin is thin.
- **Marvell/Lumentum still carries a wide deal spread.** **MRVL -12.7%** and **LITE -18.6%** Monday on the $115B all-stock announcement (4.500 fixed ratio, ~$1,132 implied, +23.9% vs the Oct 28 unaffected close).
- Both are up pre-market — MRVL +3.2%, LITE +2.4% — but at **MRVL $176.88** the implied LITE value is **$795.96** against a **$701.00** print, a **-11.9%** spread.
- Capital is locked to 1H CY28, so a persistent discount is pricing deal risk, not arbitrage.
- **The biotech tape is fading where it spiked.** **INO +213.7%** Monday on the first FDA-approved DNA medicine (VOCERYQ) is **-5.8%** pre-market; **PGEN -25.9%** Monday is **+1.8%** today;
- **DRUG -52.3%** Monday is **-9.6%** today; **KPTI -83.1%** on the Chapter 11 filing is **-6.1%** today.
- **CMPS is the exception: +6.9%** pre-market on its own Q3 — final NDA filing within two weeks, National Priority Voucher review that could compress to 1-2 months.

- **Tape breadth:** 280 names up ≥3% pre-market and 203 down ≤-3% across the US-listed universe.
- After the liquidity screen (≥100k pre-market shares, or ≥$200M cap with ≥10k shares) that is **77 up / 48 down**. This is **not a thin tape**.
- The risk is **concentration, not absence of signal**:
- the liquid pre-market decliners are dominated by Q3 software reporters (ADEA, SHOP, DT, ZBRA), while the larger percentage moves sit in sub-$5M caps whose printed pre-market liquidity is not trustworthy.

**Cluster C — AI capex financing: Oracle's $20B is the template everyone else will follow**

**Leader: ORCL (+0.6% pre-market at $119.95, after -8.8% Monday).**

- **The deal:** 86,206,897 shares at **$116.00** (11.2% below the Oct 30 close of $130.67, 2.7% below Monday's) plus **$10B of senior notes** in five tranches —
- $2.0B 7.000% due 2029, $1.75B 7.450% due 2031, $2.25B 7.850% due 2033, $2.5B 8.000% due 2037, $1.5B 8.650% due 2046 — about **$777M a year** of interest.
- Both sales close **Nov 4**.
- **Why it matters beyond Oracle:** this uses the **entire** $20B FY27-FY30 funding cap Oracle set on Oct 28, split half equity / half debt, and Oracle said in February and June it did not expect to issue bonds or debt in 2026.
- Oracle has already raised $50B this year ($25B bonds, $5B preferred, $20B stock).
- **The balance sheet behind it:** capex went from **$21.2B in FY2025 to $55.7B in FY2026**, with $28.5B spent in the August quarter alone;
- borrowings were **$125.34B** at Aug 31 plus **$288B** of lease commitments, substantially all data centres.
- Free cash flow is guided positive only in H2 FY2028, ≥$30B in FY2029, on FY2030 revenue of ≥$225B.
- **The price:** 86.2M shares is ~2.9% dilution and takes the share count back **above its June 2020 level** at a company that spent a decade shrinking it.
- At **$119.95** pre-market the market is only **+3.4%** above the $116 offering price — the dilution is priced, but the cushion is thin.

- **Read:** the AI buildout is now visibly being funded with shareholder dilution and 7-8.65% debt, and Monday's 8.8% was the market repricing **financing cost**, not AI demand.
- The corroborating read-through is **AAPL -3.9%** on memory costs and **NVDA +2.1%** —
- capital is still available for the compute, but the balance-sheet risk has moved to the platforms building the data centres.
- This is the cluster to watch for contagion: Oracle's capex is funding capacity *for AMD, Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, TikTok, xAI and others*.

**Source:** [Oracle prices $20B](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4663122-oracle-prices-20b-stock-and-bond-offering-amid-ai-expansion-sets-share-sale-at-116) · [StockTitan: share sale priced at $116](https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/oracle-stock-sale-2026-share-count-back-above-2020) · [Yahoo: $10B stock sale at $116](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/oracle-prices-10-billion-stock-121801477.html)

**Cluster D — Marvell/Lumentum: a $115B all-stock deal with a wide, persistent spread**

**Leader: LITE (the wider loser at -18.6% Monday).**

- **Ticker**: MRVL · **Nov-2 close**: 171.41 · **Nov-2 %**: -12.7% · **Pre-market**: 176.88 (+2 more column(s) in the artifact table) (row has 6 cell(s) where the header has 6)
- **Ticker**: LITE · **Nov-2 close**: 684.4 · **Nov-2 %**: -18.6% · **Pre-market**: 701.00 (+2 more column(s) in the artifact table) (row has 6 cell(s) where the header has 6)

- **The deal (8-K, Nov 2):** Marvell acquires Lumentum in an all-stock transaction. Lumentum holders receive a **fixed 4.500** MRVL shares per LITE share.
- Implied enterprise value **$115B**, implied value **~$1,132 per LITE share**, a **23.9% premium** to the Oct 28 unaffected close. Pro-forma ownership **67% MRVL / 33% LITE**. Unanimous board approval.
- Expected to close **1H CY2028**, subject to both shareholder votes and regulatory approval. Combined EV **over ~$275B**;
- companies point to a **$550B 2030 TAM**, **>$1B annual run-rate synergies** (mostly COGS), non-GAAP gross margin 57% and operating margin 39% pro-forma, accretive to MRVL non-GAAP EPS in year one.
- Matt Murphy stays CEO/Chairman; three Lumentum directors, including CEO Michael Hurlston, join the board.
- **The spread today:** at **MRVL $176.88**, the implied LITE value is **4.500 x $176.88 = $795.96**.
- LITE prints **$701.00** — a **-11.9%** discount to deal value, or **$94.96 per share** of spread.
- **Read:** both legs fell hard on the *day of* the announcement (MRVL -12.7% ,
- LITE -18.6%), which is unusual for a fixed-ratio deal where one leg should rise and the other fall.
- The market sold the acquirer for raising $115B of equity-linked consideration and sold the target because a fixed ratio hands LITE holders MRvell's price risk.
- The spread that persists is **not** arbitrage — deal capital is locked until 1H CY28 —
- so an 11.7% discount is the market pricing **deal or regulatory risk**, or doubting MRVL's own price.
- Monday's close of $171.41 was 12.7% below the unaffected $196.40: the acquirer's price *is* the spread.

**Sources:** [MRVL/LITE 8-K EX-99.1](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-26-442714/d81187dex991.htm) · [8-K EX-99.2 investor deck](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-26-442714/d81187dex992.htm) · [RTTNews on the reaction](https://www.rttnews.com/3707270/marvell-technology-stock-falls-6-after-announcing-lumentum-acquisition.aspx)

**Cluster E — Psychedelics and FDA: the winners of October are giving the gains back**

**Leader today: CMPS +6.9%.** Monday's tape was the opposite: INO +213.7%, PGEN -25.9%.

- **CMPS (the live story).** Compass Pathways reported **Q3 2026 this morning** (call 8:00 ET).
- The final **NDA submission will be filed in the next two weeks**, with rolling review already underway.
- **National Priority Voucher** review could compress the timeline to **1-2 months**, and a White House executive order directs the DEA to support rapid rescheduling after successful Phase 3 data.
- Launch remains targeted for **H1 2027**; the commercial build is in place; COMP360 should drop into an existing network of **8,500+** treatment centres.
- R&D was $23.5M vs $27.3M a year ago.
- Pre-market **$8.99, +6.9%** after **-27.3%** Monday, when a report that nonprofit Usona had filed an FDA application for psilocybin in major depression triggered fears of a faster rival path (note:
- Usona's target is MDD, COMP360 is treatment-resistant depression). Jefferies had put approval odds at 75-85%.
- **INO (the fade).** INOVIO's **VOCERYQ** — the first FDA-approved plasmid DNA immunotherapy, for recurrent respiratory papillomatosis —
- was approved on **accelerated approval** after Friday's close, with an investor call Nov 2. Monday: **+213.7%** to $1.89. Today: **-5.8%** at $1.78.
- Pricing is **~$115,000 per dose / $460,000 for the four-dose series**, shipments in ~60 days, full commercial deployment in Q1 2027 —
- and continued approval is contingent on a confirmatory study.
- **The rest of the RRP complex:** **PGEN -25.9%** Monday (direct competitor) is **+1.8%** today; **DRUG -52.3%** Monday is **-9.6%** today;
- **KPTI -83.1%** Monday (Chapter 11) is **-6.1%** today at $0.1052, on 1,694,197 pre-market shares.

- **Read:** the FDA/psychedelic complex is rotating out of the approval winner and into the commercial-catalyst names. CMPS is now the tradeable event because it has a *dated* catalyst —
- an NDA filing inside two weeks against a 1-2 month review clock —
- while INO's approval is already in the price and its risk is a confirmatory study, not a launch.

**Sources:** [Compass Pathways Q3 2026 results](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261103539380/en/) · [Compass IR: Q3 date](https://ir.compasspathways.com/News--Events-/news/news-details/2026/Compass-Pathways-to-Announce-Third-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results-on-November-3-2026/default.aspx) · [BioSpace: FDA psychedelic hearing](https://www.biospace.com/fda/psychedelic-therapies-ride-wave-of-public-favor-into-fda-hearing) · [INOVIO: FDA accelerated approval of VOCERYQ](https://ir.inovio.com/news/news-details/2026/INOVIO-Announces-FDA-Accelerated-Approval-of-VOCERYQ-an-Immunotherapy-to-Reduce-the-Frequency-of-Surgery-in-Adults-with-Recurrent-Respiratory-Papillomatosis-RRP/default.aspx) · [MedCity News on VOCERYQ](https://medcitynews.com/2026/11/inovio-voceryq-fda-approval-dna-immunotherapy-human-papillomavirus-papilloma-hpv-rrp-ino/)

**Data caveats that change how this should be read**

- **Pre-market volume on sub-$0.50 names is not trustworthy.** TV reports MERC at 118,770,409 pre-market shares and HUBC at 145,556,309 on a $0.12-$0.23 stock —
- implausible counts that inflate %ADV into the thousands of percent. Treat the sub-$1 rows in §3 and §4 as **noise, not liquidity**.
- **`premarket_time` is a constant** (the 04:00 ET session open), not the last print time, so per-name print staleness cannot be dated from the scanner.
- The pre-market snapshot is a single point in time at ~08:42 ET and will have moved by the open.
- **Every regular-session close quoted here was verified twice** —
- TradingView and the Yahoo-sourced `market-recap` agreed to the cent on all 24 names cross-checked (MRVL, LITE, AAPL, INTC, ORCL, PLTR, SHOP, FISV, AMD, NVDA, ZBRA, DT, ADEA, AEHR, LSCC, CMPS, PGEN, BLZE, DOCN, UPST, GRAB, JD, IVZ, LKNCY).
- **Catalysts are asserted only where sourced.** For a handful of smaller names (§2 Cluster F, and the mid-table of §3) no catalyst was independently sourced in this run, and none is claimed.
- **`earnings_release_next_date` is forward-looking and can be stale** for a name that reported today (it has not always rolled).
- It was used only for scheduling context, never to assert that a company reported.
- **The scanner's `in_range` filter is unreliable on a string column.** A 30-ticker `in_range` request on the `name` column returned only 14 names on the first call and a *different* subset on the second —
- silently, with no error. Every ticker quoted in this brief was therefore re-fetched with a per-ticker `equal` scan on `name`, which returns exactly one row;
- those exact rows are the source of every price and %ADV figure in §2, and the bulk pre-market screens supply the §3/§4 tables.
- A missing name in a bulk scan is a filter artefact, not a missing symbol.
- **No `mcp__*` finance tool is registered on this runtime.** Per the runtime contract that is an expected state, not an error, and it is not counted in the error count.

**11. Open research queue**

- **LITE $701.00 vs 4.500 x MRVL $176.88 = $795.96 — a -11.9% spread.** Deal capital is locked to 1H CY28, so this is not arbitrageable;
- the question for the next session is whether the discount narrows on the open or whether MRVL itself keeps falling and drags the implied value down.
- A widening spread on a rising MRVL would signal deal risk rather than sentiment.
- **ORCL $119.95 vs the $116.00 offering price — a +3.4% cushion.** Both halves of the financing close Nov 4.
- If ORCL trades below $116 the offering did not clear at the posted price and Oracle must either re-price or absorb the difference.
- **AMD's Client line is the trade.** Consensus revenue $13.08-13.09B with Q2 Client at $3.1B and Q2 Data Center at $6.7B (58% of revenue).
- A Client number near $3.1B confirms the Oct 30 PC read-through was right and the AI engine is not enough;
- a Data Center beat at ~56% GM re-rates the whole complex into Nov 4.
- **CMPS's NDA filing is the dated catalyst.** Final submission due within two weeks against a National Priority Voucher review that could compress to 1-2 months, with launch targeted for H1 2027.
- A slip past the two-week window removes the only time-bound event the name has.
- **SPX closed 7,541.40 on Nov 2 (-0.51%), already below the ~7,604 100-day average Reuters cites** (with ~7,507 as the next reference level).
- Add the election count on top of a tape where the Nasdaq-100 is in correction territory, and the 09:30 open is the first real test of whether Monday was rotation or the start of a de-risking week.
